facts.statement: The researchers used a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial design.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Twenty-one adults with persistent post-traumatic headache and no prior migraine history completed the study.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants received intravenous infusions of adrenomedullin or saline on two separate days in a random order.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The main measure was whether participants developed migraine-like headaches after receiving the drug or placebo.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Eighty-one percent of participants developed migraine-like headaches after adrenomedullin, compared to 19 percent after placebo.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Headaches started much faster after adrenomedullin (30 minutes) than after placebo (390 minutes).
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Most participants said the headaches caused by adrenomedullin felt like their usual migraine attacks.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors note that their results need to be confirmed by other studies and animal research before the pathway can be fully trusted for treatment.
facts.subject: humans
